Korean Popcorn Chicken 🍿🐔 Ingredients Chicken: • 1.1 lb (500 g) boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces • 1 egg • ½ tsp salt • ½ tsp black pepper • 1 tsp garlic powder • ½ tsp ginger powder • ½ tsp chicken bouillon • 5 tbsp cornstarch • 3 tbsp all-purpose flour Sauce: • 1.5 tbsp butter • 2 garlic cloves, minced • 1.5 tbsp gochujang • 3 tbsp ketchup • 1 tbsp soy sauce • 2 tbsp light brown sugar • 1 tbsp honey • 2 tsp rice vinegar • 1 tsp sesame oil Garnish: • Toasted sesame seeds • Sliced green onions Instructions: 1. Season the chicken with the egg, salt, black pepper, garlic powder, ginger powder, and chicken bouillon. Mix well and let rest for 10 minutes. 2. Add the cornstarch and flour, then toss until evenly coated. 3. Fry at 320–330°F (160–165°C) until cooked through. Let rest for 2–3 minutes. 4. Fry again at 355°F (180°C) until golden and crispy. 5. Melt the butter and saute the garlic until fragrant. 6. Add the gochujang, ketchup, soy sauce, light brown sugar, honey, rice vinegar, and sesame oil. Cook until glossy. 7. Toss the chicken in the sauce until evenly coated. 8. Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and sliced green onions. #chickenrecipes #koreanfood #popcorn #chicken #fyp

Kohakutou - Japanese Crystal Candy 🍬  If you’ve seen people buying the Silky Gem brand of these candies…I need you to know how cheap it is to just make them yourself at home. Recipe below! Ingredients: ½ cup water  1 tsp agar agar powder (3g) 1 cup sugar (215g) Flavor (e.g. lychee in this video)  Food coloring 1. Dissolve agar agar powder in water and bring to a simmer and stirring til dissolved.  2. Add in sugar, stir until dissolved and then mix in your desired flavouring. Simmer (small bubbles) for about 5 minutes until it thickens into a syrupy texture. Be careful not to over boil (it will spill over and make a mess). 3. Pour into a square or rectangular heat resistant container (or into candy molds) and let cool for 5-10 minutes. *Tip: if there is microfoam on top, simply use a spoon to skim it off 4. Add food coloring into whatever design or color scheme you like. 5. Cool in fridge for 2-3 hours until completely set, then remove from the container and use a knife to cut into whatever shapes you like. Tip: pile up any cuttings to form unique clusters. 6. Place on parchment paper and let dry on the counter for 4-7 days. As it dries the moisture leaves the surface and causes the sugars to crystallize, forming a crispy exterior while keeping a jelly like consistency inside! Store in airtight jars. Prepare the wet batter by whisking together buttermilk, garlic powder, black pepper, salt, and smoked paprika. Add the chicken strips to the wet batter and marinate for at least 2 hours or overnight. 2. Prepare the dry batter by whisking together flour, cornstarch, salt, garlic powder, black pepper, and smoked paprika. 3. Remove the chicken from the wet batter, allowing excess to drip off, then coat each strip in the dry batter. 4. Deep-fry the coated chicken strips in hot oil (about 350°F) until golden brown and cooked through, approximately 8-10 minutes, flipping halfway through. 5. Prepare the Cane’s Sauce by whisking together mayonnaise, ketchup,Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder, black pepper, salt, and smoked paprika. 6.
